newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-C-C Amatil now sees flat '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-C-C Amatil now sees flat '96 profit.

text.p: Australian-based beverage and snackfoods company Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd said on Friday it now believed that its net profit for the year to December 31, 1996 would show little change from the 1995 year.
It also said that trading results in the past three months had been below budget expectations.

"Coca-Cola Amatil (CCA) advised today that the company's aggressive investment programme and accelerated growth strategy have been successful in driving sales volume and market share increase, particularly in developing economies," CCA said in a statement to the stock exchange.

"This strategy has had cost and profit implications, particularly in Europe, and, given the subdued and cautious retail environment in Australia, directors now believe that the company's net profit result for the year ending December 31, 1996, will show little change with the 1995 reported result," it said.
"In forming this view, directors have taken account of trading results over the last three months, which did not achieve budget expectations."
CCA said in early August after its first half results that it expected calender 1996 profit would be 10 percent or more above the A$138.6 million recorded in calendar 1995.
CCA said it expected to report a successful year in volume, market share and per capita growth terms across all the company's 16 countries of operations.
It said its service capacity was at an all time high across all markets and that it had rebuffed efforts by competitors wanting to regain their lost market share.
CCA had invested A$800 million in plant, marketing infrastructure, vehicles and other items over 1996. It had also expanded its employee numbers from 18,000 to 25,000, with 4,000 new sales recruits.
"This accelerated employment programme is aimed at capturing still greater market share and volume growth and entrenching that growth over the long term, with ongoing momentum," it said.
CCA Chairman Dean Wills said in the statement that CCA considered the capturing of growth opportunities in emerging markets as extremely important.

"Investments we are making this year in people on the street and in the basics of building the Coca-Cola business in newer markets ensure that the CCA business world-wide is well placed to continue to deliver balanced growth and add to the worth of shareholders' investment over the coming years," Wills said.
CCA's share price closed down six cents at A$17.54 on Friday.
CCA's first half profit rose 26.1 percent to A$58.9 million.
CCA is 40 percent owned by The Coca Cola Co.
